title: "Skew normal visualization and application to deterministic Hg model (with simulated data)"
format: html

Set parameters and plot skew normal for calculating the probability of birth across the season:

1.  Calculate the PDF ($\phi$) and CDF ($\Phi$) of the skew-normal distribution for each day `x`

-   **Parameter conversion for skew-normal distribution where** $\mu$=45, $\sigma$=10, and $\alpha$ =5 **:**

$$
\begin{align*}\delta &= \frac{\alpha}{\sqrt{1 + \alpha^2}} \\\omega &= \sqrt{\frac{\sigma^2}{1 - \frac{2 \delta^2}{\pi}}} \\\xi &= \mu - \omega \delta \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}}\end{align*}
$$

2.  Multiply the PDF and CDF to obtain the joint probability of a birth happening at that specific day `x`.

$$
Pb=\frac{2}{\omega} \phi\left( \frac{x - \xi}{\omega} \right) \cdot \Phi\left( \alpha \cdot \frac{x - \xi}{\omega} \right)$$

-   **Probability density function:**
    -   $\phi( \frac{x - \xi}{\omega} )$ represents the PDF of the normal distribution at point `x` scaled by the omega parameter.
-   **Cumulative distribution function:**
    -   $\Phi\left( \alpha \cdot \frac{x - \xi}{\omega} \right)$ represents the CDF of the normal distribution up to a point shifted by $\alpha\cdot\frac{x - \xi}{\omega}$
-   **Scaling factor:**
    -   $\frac{2}{\omega}$ scales the overall probability based on the omega parameter.

```{r setup, include=TRUE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)

mu.bday=45
sd.bday=10
skew.bday=5
ndays=123
  # convert paramaters for skew normal
dskewnorm <- function(x,skew.bday,mu.bday,sd.bday) {
  
  delta <- skew.bday/sqrt(1+(skew.bday^2))
  
  omega <- sqrt(sd.bday^2/(1-(2*delta^2)/pi))
  
  xi <- mu.bday - omega*delta*sqrt(2/pi)
  (2/omega)*dnorm((x-xi)/omega) * pnorm(skew.bday*((x-xi)/omega))
}

integratePb <-  function(ndays,skew.bday,mu.bday,sd.bday) {
  # Initialize Pb as a parameter of the same length as ndays
  Pb <- rep(0, ndays)
  
  for (t in 2:ndays) {
    
    # Define the start and end of the interval
    start <- t-1   
    end <-  t
    
    # Integrate over the interval and add to the probability for this day
    Pb[t] <- Pb[t] + integrate(dskewnorm,skew.bday=skew.bday,mu.bday=mu.bday,
                               sd.bday=sd.bday, start, end)$value
    
  }
  
  # Return the probability vector
  return(Pb)
}

Pb.skewn <- integratePb(ndays,skew.bday,mu.bday,sd.bday)
sum(Pb.skewn)
plot(Pb.skewn,col="red")
```

## Visualize skew normal vs log normal

```{r,echo=FALSE}
start=32
 lCV <- sd.bday/(mu.bday-start)
 lsd <- sqrt(log(lCV^2+1))
 lmu <- log(mu.bday-start)-(0.5*(lsd^2))

 Pb.logn<-rep(0,ndays)
 # Calculate probability of being born on any given day
 for(t in 2:ndays){
   Pb.logn[t] <- plnorm((t-start+1), lmu, lsd) - plnorm((t-start), lmu, lsd)

 }

 
#Compare Pb lognorm vs skew norm
plot(Pb.logn,type="l",col="blue",xlab="Days of season",ylab="Pb.logn vs Pb.skewn")
lines(Pb.skewn,col="red")
# Legend elements
legend_labels <- c("Lognormal Pb", "Skewnormal Pb")
legend_colors <- c("blue", "red")
# Add legend at top left
legend("topright", legend_labels, fill = legend_colors, cex = 0.8)

#Compare cumulative densities
plot(cumsum(Pb.logn),type="l",col="blue",xlab="Days of season",ylab="Cumulative Density Pb.logn vs Pb.skewn")
lines(cumsum(Pb.skewn),col='red')
# Legend elements
legend_labels <- c("Lognormal Pb", "Skewnormal Pb")
legend_colors <- c("blue", "red")
# Add legend at top left
legend("topleft", legend_labels, fill = legend_colors, cex = 0.8)

```

# MODEL

Visualize gamma prior for Nborn and shifted beta priors for sd.bday, mu.bday and skew.bday:

```{r,echo=FALSE}

### shifted beta priors 
# Set parameter values

alpha.sd <- 5
beta.sd <- 5
shift.sd <- 5
scale.sd <- 7

alpha.m <- 5
beta.m <- 5
shift.m <- 10
scale.m <- 45

alpha.s <- 5
beta.s <- 5
shift.s <- 1
scale.s <- 6

# Set parameter values for the Poisson prior
lambda <- 500
# set values for Gamma prior
shape=185
scale=1

# Number of samples
n_samples <- 1000


# Generate random samples from the Gamma distribution for the Nborn prior
Nborn_prior <- rgamma(n_samples, shape,scale)

# Generate random samples from the Poisson distribution for the Nborn prior
#Nborn_prior <- rpois(n_samples, lambda)
# Generate random samples from the shifted scale beta distribution for sd.bday
sdbday.prior <- rbeta(n_samples, alpha.sd, beta.sd) * scale.sd + shift.sd

# Generate random samples for mu.bday and skew.bday
mubday.prior <- rbeta(n_samples, alpha.m, beta.m) * scale.m + shift.m


skew.prior <- rbeta(n_samples, alpha.s, beta.s) * scale.s + shift.s

# Plot 
par(mfrow=c(2,2))
par(oma=c(0,0,2,0))
# Plot density
plot(density(Nborn_prior), main = paste("Nborn prior (shape =", shape, ", scale =", scale,")", sep = ""),cex.main=0.9)
plot(density(sdbday.prior), main = paste("sd.bday (shift =", shift.sd, ", scale =", scale.sd, ", alpha =", alpha.sd, ", beta =", beta.sd, ")", sep = ""),cex.main=0.9)
plot(density(mubday.prior), main = paste("mu.bday (shift =", shift.m, ", scale =", scale.m, ", alpha =", alpha.m, ", beta =", beta.m, ")", sep = ""),cex.main=0.9)
plot(density(skew.prior), main = paste("skew.bday (shift =", shift.s, ", scale =", scale.s, ", alpha =", alpha.s, ", beta =", beta.s, ")", sep = ""),cex.main=0.9)

# quantile(Nborn_prior)
# quantile(sdbday.prior)
# quantile(mubday.prior)
# quantile(skew.prior)
```

## Results

### S3 Deterministic :

### Simulation: normal approximation using binomial variance

### Model: same as simulation

Obsdays=1:123, Nborn=500, sd.bday=10, mu.bday=45, and skew.bday=5 in simulation. Gamma prior used for Nborn, shifted beta for sd.bday, and uniform for mu.bday and skew.bday.

NOTE: this requires results from HgNimble_Model_S3.R which can be found in: S3mcmcoutput.rds

```{r,echo=FALSE}
library(bayesplot)
library(MCMCvis)

mcmcS3 <- readRDS("C:/Users/mg349/OneDrive - University of St Andrews/01 - Grey Seal Project/07 - GitHub Repositories/archive/S3mcmcoutput.rds")
# library(bayesplot)
# library(MCMCvis)
 MCMCsummary(mcmcS3,params="all")
# MCMCtrace(object = S3mcmcoutput,
#           pdf = FALSE,
#           ind = TRUE,
#           Rhat=F,
#           n.eff=F,
#           params = "all")
#MCMCplot(mcmcS4, params = 'Nborn', HPD = TRUE)
mcmc_areas(
  mcmcS3, 
  pars = "Nborn",
  prob = 0.95, # % intervals
  prob_outer = 0.99, # 99%
  point_est = "mean"
)

```
